claims.s1: Board v1.1 top pass@1 74%; 'tasks written from scratch' (paper sec 3.3).
claims.s2: Paper abstract and sec 1: SWE-bench-style fixes 'plausibly in pretraining corpora'; their tests 'can reject a valid alternative implementation or accept an incomplete one'.
claims.s3: Paper: 113 tasks, 91 repositories, five languages (TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, Rust); never merged upstream (sec 3.3).
claims.s4: Paper sec 5.2: rollouts start in a container with a shallow clone pinned to the base commit; one fixed harness, mini-swe-agent with a single bash tool and shared prompt.
claims.s5: Paper sec 3.4, 4.2: hand-written verifiers check observable behavior and accept any implementation that provides it; regression checks run on every trial.
claims.s6: Paper sec 3.4 and sec 8: disagreement rate between an LLM judge (GPT-5.5 xhigh) and each verifier; not a ground-truth error rate; small audit (30 tasks per benchmark); judge is also the top configuration in the paper.
claims.s7: Board v1.1: three setups at 74%; avg cost per task $2.36 (gemini-3.8-flash), $4.43 (gpt-6-astra), $11.84 (claude-opus-5), drawn as low/mid/high coin stacks with no figures; intervals 3, 1, 4 overlap.
claims.s8: Paper sec 1 scope and sec 8 limitations: long-horizon, multi-file implementation from a specified prompt; binary reward, no partial credit; functional correctness only; under-specified requests unmeasured; single fixed harness, not vendor tools.
